note_text:
Patient is a 52-year-old female referred for evaluation of chronic low back/buttock area discomfort of over 3 years duration. She has completed a thorough conservative treatment course including NSAIDs, gabapentin trial, activity modification with avoidance of prolonged standing, and a structured 7-month course of physical therapy focused on core stabilization and SIJ-specific exercises, all with minimal sustained benefit.

On exam, there is focal tenderness with direct palpation over the region of the posterior SI joint, reproducible and consistent on repeat exam, without tenderness of similar intensity at the greater trochanter, lumbar paraspinal region, or coccyx. No other clear pain generator identified on exam.

Provocative maneuver testing: Thigh thrust test is positive, reproducing her typical pain. Gaenslen's test and Patrick's (FABER) test are also positive. Compression test was not clearly positive.

Psychiatric review of systems is negative; no evidence of somatoform disorder or diffuse pain amplification. Tender point exam is negative for fibromyalgia; pain is not diffuse.

Imaging: Plain radiographs of the pelvis and SI joints show no destructive lesion, erosive change, or fracture. MRI of the SI joints obtained and reviewed shows no evidence of sacroiliitis, tumor, or infection. Plain film of the ipsilateral hip is unremarkable, no osteoarthritic changes. MRI of the lumbar spine was obtained and reviewed by radiology, showing no significant neural compression, disc herniation, or degenerative changes correlating with her symptoms.

She underwent two separate image-guided, contrast-enhanced diagnostic SIJ injections, performed 3 weeks apart, each of which produced greater than 75% reduction in her pain for the expected duration of the local anesthetic used, confirming the SI joint as the pain source.

Given the above workup, she is felt to be an appropriate candidate for minimally invasive percutaneous SIJ fusion, and this was discussed in detail with her including risks, benefits, and alternatives.
